correctness.rationale: Nearest-lift angular differences U,V are independent uniform(-L/2,L/2), and each vertical pair is independent uniform[0,H]. On overlap of vertical ranges length h, relative horizontal coordinate traverses a lifted interval length ell=h|U/a-V/b|<=|U|+|V|<=L. Its starting phase is Haar-uniform modulo L, yielding conditional crossing probability ell/L and at most one intersection outside null degeneracies. Averaging two centered uniform slopes of half-ranges L/(2|a|),L/(2|b|) yields 1/(4m)+m/(12M²), m=min(|a|,|b|), M=max. The normalized vertical interval-overlap kernel is J(A,B)=r s(1-s)-r³/3 with r=min(A,1-A,B,1-B) and s=max(min(A,1-A),min(B,1-B)). Integrating over 0<A<B<1 after four-region partition yields exact 65/216-2log2/9. Anisotropic scaling of x,y preserves intersections and nearest angular lifts, not a claim of isometry. The proof is exact and all-ratio.
